artifacts.summary: 4-phase implementation closed: unified resolve_goal_text() precedence chain shared by --print and --update-todo, red-then-green regression evidence, documented precedence/conflict rule, and deploy with the live active_goal/TODO.md gap closed end to end. Phase 4 closed [COMPLETED WITH EXCLUSIONS] for two sibling-owned, pre-existing deploy-gate failures unrelated to this task.

completion_data.completion_summary: Fixed generate-task-order.sh's dead active_goal read path by adding a unified resolve_goal_text() precedence chain (--goal override > non-empty active_goal > existing TODO.md Goal line > omit) shared by --print and --update-todo, removing the mode gate that previously made --print never render a Goal line at all. Added five red-then-green regression cases, documented the precedence and conflict rule in task-order-format.md/state-schema.json/state-management-schema.md, and deployed the fix, closing the live active_goal/TODO.md reproduction end to end.

memory_candidates.content: When a plan edit grows a markdown file whose line_count is tracked in an extension's index-entries.json, and that index file already carries unrelated uncommitted line_count hunks from concurrent sibling tasks, do not hand-edit the index row: git-commit-scoped.sh stages whole files (no hunk-level staging), so committing it would sweep in the siblings' unrelated changes. deploy-headless.sh automatically runs generate-context-line-counts.sh --write against the SOURCE index-entries.json (not just the deployed copy) before the deploy copy step, auto-repairing every stale entry from wc -l. Let that mechanism fix it rather than editing index-entries.json directly mid-task.

deploy-headless.sh's internal fast-gate verification (the 60s-per-gate wrapper around verify-deploy.sh's quick checks) can report a transient [FAIL] ... exceeded its 60s timeout and was killed under heavy concurrent /orchestrate batch load, even when the underlying check genuinely passes. Before writing a Reasoned Exclusion or treating it as a real regression, rerun the specific failed gate's own underlying command standalone (e.g. check-extension-docs.sh --quiet, check-task-references.sh --quiet, validate-state.sh --deep) outside the 60s wrapper; a clean standalone pass confirms the timeout was load-induced, not a content defect.
